exercises.name: Leg Press Horizontal (Machine)
depicted_equipment: continuous resistance linkage and stable frame

source_english.description: Leg Press Horizontal (Machine) presses the footplate away with both legs and lowers it until the knees are comfortably bent.
instructions: Adjust the seat and footplate so your knees are comfortably bent at the start.
Place both feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate and brace your back against the pad.
Press the plate away by extending the hips and knees without locking the knees.
Lower the plate slowly until the knees reach a comfortable bend, then repeat.
form_cues: Keep the lower back against the pad.
Track the knees over the feet.
Use the whole foot to press.
common_mistakes: Locking the knees at the top.
Allowing the hips to lift from the seat.
source_english.safety_note: Set the safety stops before loading the machine and do not descend beyond a stable back position.

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Machine)
depicted_equipment: padded distal-leg contact on a knee-extension lever
connected lever pivot and stable machine frame

source_english.description: Seated at the leg-extension machine, straighten the knees to lift the pad and lower it with control.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and backrest of the machine to fit your body.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet on the footpad.
Grasp the handles or sidebars for stability.
Extend your legs forward by straightening your knees, lifting the weight.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the thigh against the seat while the lower leg straightens.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

exercises.name: Hip Adduction (Machine)
depicted_equipment: paired medial-thigh contact pads on connected moving arms

source_english.description: Seated with the back supported, press the machine pads together to bring the thighs toward the midline.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the backrest.
Place your feet on the footrests and grasp the handles for stability.
Engage your adductor muscles and slowly bring your legs together, squeezing your inner thighs.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the pelvis against the pad while the knees move together.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Machine)
depicted_equipment: two graspable handles on connected fly arms

source_english.description: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Machine) moves the arms outward and back through a controlled rear-delt fly arc with the chest supported on the machine pad.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms slightly bent.
Exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the handles back and outward, away from your body.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and stop if the shoulder cannot move smoothly.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Cable)
depicted_equipment: continuous cable routed through high pulley to resistance

source_english.description: Lat Pulldown (Cable) pulls the band, cable bar, or machine handles from overhead toward the upper chest while the torso stays braced.
instructions: Adjust the cable pulldown machine so that the seat is at a comfortable height and the knee pad is secured.
Sit on the seat with your back straight and your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the cable bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lean back slightly and engage your core.
Pull the cable bar down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the ribs stacked and shoulders down.
Drive the elbows toward the torso.
Control the return to the start.
common_mistakes: Leaning or swinging to move the load.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure station and a load or assistance level you can control through the full range.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row - V Grip (Cable)
exercises.equipment_type: seated low-pulley V-handle cable row station

source_english.description: Sit with feet braced at the low pulley, grip the close V handle neutrally, and pull it toward the navel before extending the arms.
instructions: Sit at a low cable pulley with feet on the footplate, knees softly bent, and torso upright.
Hold the close V handle with palms facing each other.
Pull the handle to the navel while drawing both elbows behind the ribs.
Let the arms extend fully without rounding the back.
form_cues: Keep the chest supported or torso upright.
Drive the elbows toward the ribs.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest from the pad.
Shrugging instead of pulling the elbows.
Letting the weight fall on return.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the torso supported or upright so the shoulder is not jerked by the cable or bar.

exercises.name: Triceps Rope Pushdown
depicted_equipment: high pulley on stable cable station
two-ended rope attachment with secure end grips
complete station base and resistance connection

source_english.description: Triceps Rope Pushdown uses a high-pulley rope, extending both elbows while the rope ends separate slightly at the bottom.
instructions: Stand facing the high pulley with feet shoulder-width apart and knees softly bent.
Grip the rope with a neutral grip with elbows beside the ribs.
Press the attachment down until the elbows are straight without leaning over it.
Pause at the bottom, then allow the elbows to bend until the forearms return to the start.
source_english.safety_note: Set the pulley and attachment securely and use resistance that keeps the elbows close.
